messages:
maya: Heads up — after yesterday's OFED + mlx5 FW rollout in us-west2 we started seeing NCCL allreduce bandwidth drop on Pod groups pinned across two racks. Metrics: 2-3x token-generation tail latency and ~40-60% lower inter-node bw. Logging it here so infra team can correlate.

arjun: ugh, which FW and OFED versions did we push?

maya: OFED 5.7.1 / MLX5 FW 16.30.1000 (rolled from 16.28). Kernel on hosts is 5.15.0-1026. We only rolled ~120 nodes in the anchor pool (g5/8-type machines).

sophia: any packet drops or errors on the mlx devices? ifindex errors?

maya: checked dmesg + `ethtool -S eth0` on a few nodes — big increase in `mlx5_core` rx_errors and `tx_err`. Also `ibv_rc_pingpong` shows asymmetric BW: one node 11000 MB/s, peer 2600 MB/s.

devon: can you paste the ibv_devinfo and firmware version output?

maya: pasted below:
```
$ ibv_devinfo -v
hca_id: mlx5_0
firmware_ver: 16.30.1000
node_guid: 0x248a07fffe123456
vendor_part_id: 4100
```

and `ethtool -S eth0 | grep -E "err|drop|rx"` shows lots of `rx_crc_errors` on the bad NICs.

arjun: this smells like a firmware <-> kernel <-> mlx5 driver ABI regression. We bumped the MLX5 FW and the OFED stack recently. Did we also push a new kernel module build?

maya: we didn't touch kernel modules; OFED package upgraded the userspace libs and kernel modules (mlx5, rdma-core), but kernels stayed the same.

sophia: NCCL logs show retries and fallback to TCP for some collectives?

maya: yes — NCCL info shows `Network mutex timed out, fallback to tcp`. All-reduce falls back and throughput tanks.

infra-oncall: tagging @eng-sre. Can we isolate to hardware subset? region-wide?

maya: confined to us-west2, and only the nodes that were in the first rollout batch (rack A, racks A1-A3). Other racks with older FW are fine.

arjun: immediate mitigation: revert FW on the affected nodes or roll them back to previous OFED package. Reboot required either way. What's the risk to running workloads if we leave them?

devon: degraded throughput, higher cost (because of more GPUs per job to hit SLAs) and increased tail latencies. Jobs still complete but slower; models with allreduce timings miss SLO. I'd prefer rollback for canary nodes.

sophia: can we NAK traffic between bad pairs to avoid cross-rack collective mix that triggers NCCL fallback? maybe route policy to keep collectives local temporarily.

arjun: we can add a temporary placement constraint: prefer intra-rack scheduling for gang-scheduled workloads, and mark affected nodes as `avoid-gpu` in k8s. That buys time for rollback.

maya: making a list of affected node IDs now: host-uw2-a-0{12..27} and -a-40,41.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 — "mlx5 fw/OFED causing NCCL degradation us-west2" assigned to eng-infra. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0423

infra-oncall: Plan: 1) isolate affected nodes (cordon + drain), 2) rollback OFED package to 5.6.x release and downgrade mlx5 FW where possible, 3) run `ib_read_bw` and NCCL benchmarks, 4) monitor cost/slowness dashboards. Schedule maintenance window in 30m.

arjun: test commands we should run after rollback:
```
# check kernel module
modinfo mlx5_core | grep firmware
# kernel IB info
ibv_devinfo -v
# bandwidth tests
ib_read_bw -d mlx5_0
# nccl test
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO python -m tests.nccl_allreduce
```

devon: if firmware downgrade is blocked by vendor restrictions, we need to escalate to networking vendor for a microcode compatibility patch. Also check driver ABI between kernel module and userspace rdma-core (`rdma-core` package version).

sophia: also capture tcpdump + `perf record -e net:*` on a bad pair during a short run to see retransmits pattern. Might be HW-level CRCs.

maya: rolling back OFED on 5 nodes now as canary. I'll report results in ~15m.

(15m later)

maya: canary results: after downgrading OFED and reloading mlx5 module, `ib_read_bw` back to expected 10-11 GB/s symmetric across the pair. NCCL allreduce throughput restored and no more fallback.

arjun: great. Proceed with staged rollback across all affected nodes. Coordinate with oncall and schedule 2hr window per rack.

infra-oncall: are there any plans to reattempt upgraded FW? we should open a test pool to iterate with vendor FW + kernel module variants before rolling again.

sophia: yes — create a dedicated lab cluster with mixed kernel versions (5.15 and 6.1), rdma-core variants, and multiple mlx5 FW versions. Run long-duration nccl+ib benchmarks, plus real model traces.

maya: filing a postmortem checklist in #postmortems after rollback. Immediate action items: 1) complete rollback across us-west2, 2) label affected nodes, 3) create vendor escalation, 4) bake test pool.

arjun: add cost impact calc: about 18% increase in GPU-hours for affected jobs last 24h estimated $15k. Include in PM.

ops-bot: Update: INC-2026-0423 status -> Mitigated.

maya: thanks everyone. I'll ping when full fleet rollback completes. :thumbsup:
